_meta.description: Every question about Blip: what it needs, Intel Macs, the iPhone and iPad app, Homebrew, Blip Helper, memory use, privacy, price and availability.
a-mac-with-apple.8d5a83: A Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 14 Sonoma or later, or an iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later.
blip-is-built-exclusively.784fc9: Blip is built exclusively for Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4 and newer). It uses ARM64-specific optimizations and Apple Silicon IOKit interfaces for GPU and thermal monitoring.
built-by-blaine-miller.9d6375: Built by Blaine Miller · Open Source under MIT License
can-i-customize-what.f3b410: Can I customize what shows in the menu bar?
can-i-install-it.9ac23d: Can I install it with Homebrew?
clone-the-repo-install.bd6619: Clone the repo, install XcodeGen (brew install xcodegen), run xcodegen generate, then build with Xcode or xcodebuild. See the README for full instructions.
does-blip-work-on.0c1c57: Does Blip work on Intel Macs?
everything-people-ask-about.b4b9b0: Everything people ask about Blip on the Mac, iPhone and iPad.
hover-over-any-row.3e9db5: Hover over any row in the main popover to reveal a detailed sub-panel to the side — just like iStats Menus. It shows charts, breakdowns, and top processes for that category.
how-do-i-build.5e186c: How do I build from source?
how-does-the-hover.65453d: How does the hover detail panel work?
how-much-memory-does.a1c4d1: How much memory does Blip use?
is-blip-available-in.3bdff6: Is Blip available in the European Union?
is-there-an-iphone.q77001: Is there an iPhone and iPad app?
the-app-store-keeps.416fd4: The App Store keeps Mac apps in a sandbox, so fans, temperatures, GPU, disk I/O, battery health and top processes come through the free Blip Helper. The direct download reads them itself.
typically-around-42-mb.7ba8b7: Typically around 42 MB physical footprint. Blip shows its own memory usage in the popover footer so you can always check. The binary itself is around 2 MB.
what-do-i-need.c6c81a: What do I need to run it?
why-do-some-mac.0e11f5: Why do some Mac stats need Blip Helper?
yes-blip-is-on.991f87: Yes. Blip is on the App Store everywhere in the European Union, France included, and the direct download and Homebrew cask work everywhere.
yes-blip-is-open.45f52c: Yes. Blip is open source and every Mac release is notarized by Apple. There are no analytics, no crash reporters and no servers: everything runs on your device.
yes-blip-stats-2.q77002: Yes — Blip Stats 2.0 is one free app across Mac, iPhone, and iPad. The iOS app shows live device stats with drill-in details, runs Blip Bench (including the Neural Engine), tests network and disk speed, does ping and traceroute with an offline hop map, and ships Home Screen widgets and Shortcuts.
yes-brew-install-cask.730725: Yes: brew install --cask blaineam/tap/blip installs the direct-download Mac app.
yes-on-every-platform.f595c8: Yes, on every platform. The App Store app for Mac, iPhone and iPad, the direct download and the Homebrew cask are all free, with nothing to unlock.
yes-open-settings-from.0f7be7: Yes. Open Settings from the gear in the popover and choose which items show: CPU, Memory, Disk, GPU and the network dot, with or without labels, in a horizontal or stacked layout and the colors you like.
your-devices-vitals-at.cb380c: Your devices' vitals, at a glance.
